contract-requirements.note: No motion/API-CONTRACT.md exists in this worktree. The following must be frozen by the coordinator before rig/pose workers can bind to these scene anchors.

items.detail: Freeze the set of valid anchor ids and their world coordinates. This layout proposes: counter-front, counter-top, tray, coin-hand, coin-lift, coin-tray-land, slot, washer-drum-nearest, rear-door, rear-door-gaze, lamp, lamp-spill, cloth-pivot, cel-standing, walk-start, walk-mid, walk-arrive, counter-pose, half-step-back, at-washer.

Define whether character position is tracked at head-center (690,925), hip-center (~690,1107), or foot-contact (~690,1280), and in world or local coords. This layout uses world coords and provides all three.

The floor at counter depth is approximately y=1280 (consistent with INTERFACE.md body-to-y1290 for a character with ~10px toe offset). Contract must state the canonical foot-plant y for the counter standing position.

Current main.mjs clips ALL of the SVG layer below y=1110 globally. The plan requires position-based occlusion: clip only when cel rootX is within the counter x-range [~600,760]. Coordinator must decide: (a) modify nunClip to be position-dependent, (b) move character to Canvas layer for some shots, or (c) accept global clip. This affects full-body walking in cue 2.

Cue 2 describes 2-3 steps from washer area to counter. If the cel starts at x~480 (left of counter), the current y=1110 global clip hides the lower body even though the counter is NOT between the camera and the character. Coordinator must specify how the renderer handles full-body visibility during the walk.

Contact shadows under feet are at y~1280 (below the y=1110 SVG clip). They must render on the Canvas layer, not SVG. Coordinator must specify the draw order and compositing mode for these shadows relative to the environment and character layers.

occlusion.mjs exports a lightingGrade(rootX, rootY) helper returning warm/cool/ambient/rim intensities. The contract must specify what format the renderer expects and how it composites the grade (e.g., feComponentTransfer slopes, overlay opacity, etc.).
